title: Annual Flood Premium on File for the Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve
content:
1. **Subject.** Under Set-Aside Accounts, this rule sets the annual flood premium held on a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve, called here the projected annual flood premium, whenever the flood insurance bills on file are reviewed.
2. **Scope.** For a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve, and only for such a reserve, the annual flood premium held on file is the projected annual flood premium rather than the billed amount of the current flood policy term. The annual flood premium of every other set-aside remains under the general annual-charges rule of Set-Aside Accounts.
3. **Recording.** The figure is recorded with `update_reserve_flood_ec384f8d`, which the servicing agent unlocks and then calls. The tool records a new annual flood insurance premium on a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve after a review of the flood insurance bills on file: it replaces the annual flood premium held on the reserve with the figure supplied and leaves the reserve balance, its ledger, the bills on file and the annual property tax and hazard premium unchanged. Afterwards the reserve shows the new annual flood premium to anyone who looks it up.
4. **Parameters.**

| Name | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `setaside_id` | Reference number of the Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve whose annual flood premium is replaced, as the set-aside account lookup returns it for the loan | Identifier |
| `setaside_request_id` | Reference number of the flood insurance bill on file that the review relied on, as the set-aside bills and requests lookup returns it for that reserve | Identifier |
| `annual_flood_premium` | The annual flood premium to hold on the reserve | USD, 2 decimal places, positive, already rounded to the cent before the call |

5. **Receipt.** `status` reads "updated" when the figure was recorded, with `setaside_id`, `setaside_request_id` (the bill relied on), `previous_annual_flood_premium` (held before the call) and `annual_flood_premium` (now held), amounts to 2 decimal places.
